message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of the clade that contains the families **Felidae** (cats) and **Equidae** (horses, zebras, etc.).  
That clade is the one that contains the orders **Carnivora** (which includes lions) and **Perissodactyla** (which includes zebras).  
In turn, the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the superorders **Laurasiatheria**.  

So, in short, the most recent common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the superorders Laurasiatheria (i.e., the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla).
